citation.title: Machine Learning based parameter tuning strategy for MMC based topology optimization
citation.authors: Xinchao Jiang, Hu Wang, Yu Li, Kangjia Mo
citation.venue: Advances in Engineering Software, vol. 149, art. 102841 (published 2020-11, Crossref metadata checked 2026-09-24); arXiv preprint
citation.version_coded: arXiv v1 (submitted 16 Oct 2019; only version on the abs page), full text read from the PDF (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.07227). The version of record (ScienceDirect, PII S0965997820300363) was attempted via the doi.org and Elsevier link-resolver chain; the ScienceDirect article page returned HTTP 403 with a CAPTCHA challenge to an anonymous request and was not read further (no bot check bypassed).

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Not coded (excluded). Headline: an Extra-Trees image classifier, trained on Bag-of-Visual-Words features of MMC-based solutions labeled feasible/infeasible, is embedded in a closed loop with Particle Swarm Optimization to auto-tune the MMA optimizer's parameters; on two 2D compliance-minimization cases (cantilever, L-shape beam) it reaches a feasible optimum (C = 74.02 and C = 183.76) without manual parameter tuning.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not coded (excluded at full text). No classical, non-learned parameter-tuning or TO baseline is run, timed or cited anywhere in the article; the motivation ('parameters are tuned according to the experience', 'saves a lot of manpower') is qualitative only, with no measured manual-tuning time, iteration count or cost figure given for comparison. The only quantitative comparisons in the article (Tables 4 and 7, Sec. 4.2: P, R, F1, ACC, AUC, P-R and ROC plots) are among four machine-learning classifiers -- Extra-Trees, Random Forest, AdaBoost, GradientBoost -- for feasibility-classification quality, not a classical TO comparator.

notes: Excluded under PROTOCOL Sec.4 and the FT-MLONLY full-text exclusion code (screening_codes.md, second table): the article's only quantitative comparisons are among four machine-learning classifiers (Extra-Trees, Random Forest, AdaBoost, GradientBoost; Tables 4 and 7, Sec. 4.2) for feasibility-classification quality (P, R, F1, ACC, AUC; P-R and ROC plots, Figs. 9 and 12). No classical, non-learned TO or parameter-tuning method (e.g. default/manually tuned MMC-TO, SIMP) is run, timed or cited with a comparable cost or result anywhere in the article. Two compliance-minimization cases are solved with the proposed closed loop (cantilever, 40x80-element mesh, C=74.02 at iteration ~67, Table 5/Fig. 10; L-shape beam, 4864-element mesh, C=183.76 at iteration ~62, Table 8/Fig. 13), but neither is compared against a non-ML-tuned run of the same problem, and no wall-clock times are reported for any run. Secondary reason for the verifier: FT-NOBASELINE is also defensible on the same facts (no classical method's cost or result is run, timed or cited at all, so 'no comparison of any kind' also holds); FT-MLONLY is used here because table order (screening_codes.md) places it before FT-NOBASELINE and the article does perform a quantitative comparison, confined to ML methods. included.method_family is 'other' because Extremely Randomized Trees is a tree-ensemble classifier, not covered by the schema's cnn/gan/vae/diffusion_flow/transformer/gnn/llm_agent/rl/neural_reparam/surrogate_mlp_gp categories. Physics is mini-compliance in both cases (Sec. 4.2, 4.2 [L-shape numbered as a second '4.2' in the PDF]); dim is 2d (40x80 and 4864-element planar meshes).
